title: Deep Blue won with speed plus evaluation, not learning
body: IBM's Deep Blue, which beat Kasparov in 1997, searched on the order of two hundred million positions per second with hand-tuned evaluation on custom chips. It did not learn from its games. Its victory closed the brute-force chapter of chess AI just before learning methods opened another, quieter and stranger one.
source_hint: Campbell, Hoane, Hsu (2002), Deep Blue paper
